observations:
Torah #136 contains three thematic packages (see torah_136_packages.json), all of which are contained within the standard package taxonomy established across Likutay Moharan:

  Package 1 — דָּן לְכַף זְכוּת וְדִין אֱמֶת (good): Favorable judgment as true justice. This is a classic Rebbe Nachman good-practice cluster: a spiritual/ethical act (judging favorably) is identified with a divine quality (judgment/justice). This pattern recurs throughout LM1 — see Torah #282 (לְכַף זְכוּת), Torah #2 (מִשְׁפָּט), and numerous others. No novel package type needed.

  Package 2 — מָקוֹם וּמַדְרֵגָה (neutral): Place and spiritual level as structural equivalents. This is an interpretive re-reading of the Mishnah's 'place' as 'level'. While the specific equation מָקוֹם=מַדְרֵגָה is unique to this Torah's framing, the structural pattern (reinterpreting a spatial term as a spiritual dimension) is a standard Rebbe Nachman device. No novel package type needed.

  Package 3 — מַחֲלֹקֶת (evil): Conflict/dispute as the negative force. This is a standard evil-domain package. Machlokes appears as an evil concept in many LM1 Torahs (e.g., Torah #33, Torah #46, Torah #80 ff.). No novel package type needed.

The Torah's good/evil mirror structure is minimal but present:
- Package 1 (judging favorably = justice) is the exact positive counterforce to Package 3 (conflict = injustice/separation). The same evaluative act — seeing a person — is either the source of machlokes (when one judges by difference/shortcoming) or the source of peace and elevation (when one judges favorably). This is the mirror.

The Torah is notably short and conceptually economical. It presents a single argument with three moving parts: the problem (machlokes from difference in level), the structural condition for resolution (equality in level), and the practice that achieves it (favorable judgment = actual justice that elevates). All three map cleanly onto the three packages. No independent conceptual domain emerged that would require a fourth package or a new package type not seen elsewhere in LM1.
